title: Crafting
summary: The Artisan Bench, how recipes unlock, the gear ladders, tool tiers and which blocks pay out.

s.x: Almost all SkyRPG gear is crafted at the

. Unlike the vanilla crafting grid, it asks for exact counts ("32 Skyiron Ingots"), locks recipes behind skill levels, and takes the old item as an ingredient so upgrades keep their enchantments. This page covers the bench, the gear ladders it builds, tool tiers and the placed-block rules.
is a block you can place anywhere. Get one by:
Crafting it at a crafting table: a crafting table in the middle, 4 iron ingots on the edges and 4 Glimmer Crystals in the corners.
Buying one from Dorrin Saltmarsh at Saltmarsh Provisions for 1,500 coins.
Right-click it to open the crafting screen. Admins can open it anywhere with
, and NPCs can open it too.
Before you have your own, use the public bench in Skyhaven: it stands in the Emberforge yard, next to Brannoc Ashforge (by the smithing table). It's the only bench you can use in the hub.
There is a tab for each kind of recipe (backpacks, combat, cooking, dungeon, farming, fishing, foraging, mining, region and slayer), plus an All tab.
Every recipe shows its result, its ingredients (red where you are short) and the level it needs. Locked recipes say what they need, for example "Mining 18" or "Coal Collection V".
crafts as many as you can afford, up to 64 at once.
Ingredients come from your inventory and from inside your carried backpacks.
Recipes unlock as your skill levels rise, and the level-up message lists the new ones ("NEW RECIPES at the Artisan Bench").
Most gear recipes take the previous piece as their first ingredient. The result keeps the old item's
custom name, enchantments, lore and contents

, so a backpack keeps what is inside it and a pickaxe keeps its Prosperity (SkyRPG enchants and all). The new tool comes fully repaired, so upgrading also mends a worn one. Only SkyRPG tools, armour, accessories and backpacks count as the item being upgraded.
A handful of recipes also need a collection tier (see
). The recipe shows "Requires Skyiron Collection III" while it is locked.
Some things stay at the normal crafting table and show in the recipe book:

(string, leather and an iron ingot) and the starter gear: the Prospector set and pickaxe (stone, iron), the Harvester set and hoe (hay blocks), the Woodsman set and axe (logs) and the Vanguard set (iron and redstone blocks).

Compacting: 9 Glimmer Shards make a Glimmer Crystal, 9 Dewdrops a Dew Vial, 9 Tidescales a Tidescale Plate, 9 Heartwood Splinters a Heartwood Bundle, 9 Valor Marks a Valor Seal, and each reverses. Skyiron Ingots, Emberite Ingots and Duskquartz Shards pack into blocks.
Smelting: Raw Skyiron in a furnace or blast furnace, Emberite Chunks and Hellforged Scrap in a blast furnace only.
Planks of the five new woods, which work in every vanilla wood recipe.

You cannot farm XP by placing blocks and breaking them again. The game remembers every block a player places, and a placed block gives
no skill XP, no Glimmer Shards, no rare finds, no event points and no contract progress

Some things pay out even when you place them, because placing them is how you use them: crops and saplings, sugar cane, cactus, cocoa, nether wart, bamboo, sweet berry bushes, melon and pumpkin stems, kelp, mushrooms, mining nodes, foraging stumps and planters. (A melon or pumpkin block you placed still gives nothing.) Treefeller also never fells logs you placed.

Nodes, stumps and planters are the safe way to get a steady income of Glimmer, Heartwood and Dew while you are away from the big world. They are cheaper XP than ores, so mix them with real mining, chopping and farming.
